content.short_description: Big Rigs: The Yellow Cab (2005) - A poorly-received title with fundamental design issues that prevented critical success.
content.reviewer_notes: Total 90/100; strongest pillar is values, with accessibility as the main score limiter.
content.values_findings: Big Rigs: The Yellow Cab exemplifies responsible monetization with premium pricing and zero exploitative mechanics. Launched at $24.99. No day-one microtransactions. No loot boxes or randomized paid rewards.
content.ethics_findings: Big Rigs: The Yellow Cab demonstrates strong ethical practices including honest marketing and good post-launch support. Announced well ahead of 2005 release. Post-launch support sustained.
content.gameplay_findings: Big Rigs: The Yellow Cab provides exceptional gameplay depth with substantial campaign and multiple meaningful outcomes. Designed as single-player experience. Multiplayer features added post-launch. Multiple endings reward different playstyles.
content.accessibility_findings: Big Rigs: The Yellow Cab provides comprehensive accessibility including multiple control schemes and localization. Multi-language localization included.
content.standards_findings: Big Rigs: The Yellow Cab achieves solid technical quality with good launch reception and feature completeness. Fully offline-playable campaign. Legacy release exemption applied (pre-2010).
